rule: Facts about candidate gameplay/structure only. Critic numeric verdicts are not used as user preference evidence or prediction targets.

games.title: Assassin's Creed
facts: third-person historical action/stealth built around climbing, freerunning and target assassinations
investigation-to-assassination structure repeats heavily across targets
visual/world presentation and traversal provide a distinct initial hook

games.title: Borderlands
facts: first-person shooting is paired with RPG leveling, skill trees and constant randomized loot
combat and reward progression form the central loop
quest structure and enemy patterns can become repetitive, especially solo

games.title: Castlevania: Lords of Shadow
facts: linear action-adventure mixing combo-heavy combat, platforming and environmental puzzles
new skills/subweapons are introduced over time; bosses demand use of core combat tools
restricted exploration, intrusive hints/QTEs can interrupt agency

games.title: Cyberpunk 2077
facts: first-person open-world action RPG with combat, stealth/hacking and character progression
main characters and side quests are a major narrative focus
large city/open-world structure can contain unevenly meaningful ambient content

games.title: Darksiders
facts: action-adventure with fluid combat, exploration and Zelda-like environmental puzzles
new items and mechanics regularly open paths and puzzle solutions
story is comparatively thin; controls can be overcomplicated

games.title: Grand Theft Auto III
facts: open clockwork city supports free roaming and systemic mayhem
73 story missions provide directed progression while remaining optional between free-roam periods
vehicle/on-foot sandbox is central

games.title: Grand Theft Auto V
facts: large varied open world with many side activities
three protagonists can be switched within elaborate multi-stage missions
mission design frequently changes roles and scenarios

games.title: Half-Life: Blue Shift
facts: short Half-Life expansion with straightforward firefights, jumping puzzles and a Xen segment
adds few fundamentally new challenges relative to Half-Life
best understood as a compact alternate-perspective return to Black Mesa

games.title: Hogwarts Legacy
facts: spell combat and Hogwarts exploration are the strongest distinctive systems
castle contains puzzles, activity and environmental detail
large outside open world relies heavily on repetitive checklist tasks; combat and progression can become repetitive

games.title: Lucius II
facts: each level is structured as a sandbox for choosing how and whom to kill
supernatural abilities support multiple approaches
reported technical/AI problems and repetition can undermine the sandbox

games.title: Mafia II
facts: story-led crime action with a detailed city
strong narrative/action focus
open city is underused and offers little meaningful side content

games.title: Marvel's Spider-Man
facts: web-swinging traversal has an accessible but expressive movement system
acrobatic combat expands through skills/gadgets and supports some stealth
story and superhero identity are prominent while recurring city crimes/activities repeat

games.title: Mass Effect
facts: story-driven sci-fi RPG with engaging party characters and branching dialogue
combat and skill management support character builds
exploration/quests sit inside a broad galaxy narrative

games.title: Mirror's Edge
facts: first-person parkour centered on speed, momentum and precise traversal
mastery comes from chaining movement and replaying routes
tedious jumping puzzles, unclear objectives and combat interruptions can break flow

games.title: Need for Speed: Most Wanted
facts: street racing career organized around the Blacklist
police pursuits add escalating pressure, roadblocks and tactical escape play
core racing is familiar but chases materially diversify the loop

games.title: Perfect World
facts: MMORPG built around questing/leveling, skill progression and extensive character customization
movement includes flight and a large persistent world
contemporary player reports describe both broad content and potential grind/repetition

games.title: Postal 2
facts: free-roaming first-person city structured around daily errands
allows non-linear/violent sandbox interaction but core systems are shallow
technical loading and repetition can heavily interrupt exploration

games.title: Prince of Persia: Warrior Within
facts: parkour/platforming remains central while combat is deeper and more free-form than Sands of Time
dual wielding and combo options expand combat expression
darker, more serious tone; backtracking/repetition can be friction

games.title: Prototype
facts: fast-paced open-world action built around extreme agility and superpowers
varied missions and boss battles support frequent action changes
story mystery provides forward momentum

games.title: Red Dead Redemption
facts: large lively Western open world with random encounters and optional activities
linear central story can be paused for exploration
story missions and side activities are varied and tied to character/world immersion

games.title: Resident Evil 4
facts: third-person horror-action with deliberately paced shooting
frequent set-pieces/bosses and clear forward direction maintain momentum
long adventure includes secrets and bonus content, with sustained action variety

games.title: Sanitarium
facts: story-led point-and-click adventure with psychologically surreal settings
puzzles are integrated into narrative and atmosphere
pixel hunting, mazes and some unclear interactions can create friction

games.title: Tekken 3
facts: 3D fighting game with large roster, deep move/combo sets and multiple modes
mastery differs by character and rewards practice
extra modes broaden the loop beyond ordinary arcade fights

games.title: The Banner Saga 2
facts: turn-based tactical combat emphasizes positioning, armor/health tradeoffs and unit abilities
strategic caravan decisions feed narrative consequences
refines the first game's systems but is narratively dependent on prior context

games.title: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion
facts: large open-ended RPG with extensive character customization and exploration
many guilds, side quests and activities support different play styles
quest tracking gives clear goals despite the world's breadth

games.title: The Exit 8
facts: short first-person observation/walking game set in a repeating corridor
progress depends on detecting visual/environmental anomalies and deciding whether to turn back
deliberate repetition is the core mechanic rather than broad mechanical progression

games.title: The Suffering
facts: horror-themed action game that favors fast combat over slow survival-horror resource management
creature design and visual scares create atmosphere
straightforward structure and limited enemy/tactical variety can become repetitive

games.title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Blood and Wine
facts: large new Toussaint region with a vivid visual identity and many quests
mixes story, exploration, combat and side content over a substantial expansion
new region and mysteries provide a stronger sense of novelty than a small add-on

games.title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Hearts of Stone
facts: compact story-focused expansion built around character-rich branching quests
story subverts expectations and uses varied combat/non-combat quest situations
some minigame/detective passages interrupt pacing

games.title: WarCraft 3: The Frozen Throne
facts: expansion adds multiple campaigns, units, heroes and substantial mechanical depth
campaign missions deliberately vary objectives and often depart from standard base-building
bonus campaign shifts toward hero-led RPG-like exploration
